steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Asymmetric Looped Transformers: Fixed Global Representations for an Iterative Decoder
summary: It replaces full-stack layer looping, where one shared recurrent block both builds context and refines state, with a single-pass causal encoder producing fixed global KV caches plus a weight-tied recurrent decoder attending jointly to global and local KV. The cost is an architecture change requiring training from scratch, including a heavy-tail-guided layerwise learning-rate schedule, and some extra memory for per-layer global KV caches; there is no inference-time drop-in benefit. It can fail if the fixed-context/separate-refinement gains do not transfer beyond the FineWeb-Edu pretraining regime tested, and the absolute quality gain (~1.3 accuracy points) is modest relative to retraining cost.
rationale: The method is a pretraining architecture requiring foundation-model training that the reader's constrained infrastructure explicitly excludes, so it is worth tracking but not adoptable now.
technique: Asymmetric looped transformer with fixed global KV

claims.statement: It replaces full-stack layer looping, where one shared recurrent block both builds context and refines state, with a single-pass causal encoder producing fixed global KV caches plus a weight-tied recurrent decoder attending jointly to global and local KV. The cost is an architecture change requiring training from scratch, including a heavy-tail-guided layerwise learning-rate schedule, and some extra memory for per-layer global KV caches; there is no inference-time drop-in benefit. It can fail if the fixed-context/separate-refinement gains do not transfer beyond the FineWeb-Edu pretraining regime tested, and the absolute quality gain (~1.3 accuracy points) is modest relative to retraining cost.

At 1B scale, average zero-shot accuracy across seven commonsense benchmarks rises from 49.58% to 50.85% versus Full Loop under matched effective depth and token budget, with consistently lower validation perplexity from 60M to 1B.
